summary: Authoring contract for email drafting (no sender, list or send capability is implied): single emails, new-subscriber welcome sequences, new-customer onboarding sequences and promotion sequences planned backwards from an approved closing date; honest subject and preview options, one job and one action per email, value between asks, urgency only from approved terms, and all claims bound to verified facts.

requiredInputs.purpose: Sequence purpose, position in sequence, audience segment, desired single action, length limit.
Runtime statement of the recipient relationship (for example existing customer, consented subscriber) supplied by the owner; the pack never infers it.
Destinations the action may point at.
Single email (default), new-subscriber welcome sequence, new-customer onboarding sequence, or promotion sequence.
For a promotion sequence: the approved start and end dates and any approved deadline terms.
Existing approved articles or resources a sequence may link to as value between asks.

decisionSteps.instruction: When sequenceKind is a sequence, map every email before writing any: its position, its single job, its proposed send timing relative to the trigger, and its single action. A welcome sequence moves from delivering what was promised, to who the brand is, to one useful lesson, to what good looks like (illustrative or permissioned), to one invitation. An onboarding sequence moves from confirming the purchase, to the fastest first useful step, to what to expect, to a permissioned success example or an illustrative one, to the natural next offer only if approved. A promotion sequence is planned from its approved closing date backwards: interest check, opening, value between asks, objection answers, closing reminder, final notice, and a post-close follow-up; the number of emails follows the window length and the owner's stated frequency, never a fixed count.

State in one sentence what this email must achieve for the reader and where it sits in the sequence (first contact, follow-up, value delivery, offer, reminder). Record what the previous email in the sequence covered if supplied.

Write three to five subject lines that each describe the actual content from a different entry point (the question answered, the benefit, the situation, the plain description) plus a short preview line that continues the subject truthfully. No deception, no fake replies, no urgency without an approved date.

Open with the reason this reader is receiving the email now; deliver the value or information in short paragraphs; close with one next action. Decide whether a short reassurance about frequency or opt-out belongs in the body (the platform footer handles legal elements; do not duplicate them).
Apply production-core's single next action, phrased for a reader who will act from their inbox, pointing at a linkable page or an explicit reply instruction.

For a sequence, state in the sidecar which existing measures the owner can read afterwards (opens, clicks, replies, completions) and what each would suggest changing; give no target percentages, benchmarks or pivot thresholds, because none are evidence for this brand.

Hand the draft to the existing approval path only. There is no send step in this pack: if the runtime has no email drafting or sending path for this brand, the draft is saved as held and the sidecar says so.

rules.instruction: The subject line describes what the body delivers. 'Re:' prefixes, fake forwards, questions the body does not answer and bracketed urgency are forbidden.
rules.check: Each subject's promise is fulfilled in the body.

rules.instruction: The body never asserts a relationship the permissionContext does not state ('as a valued customer' only if the context says customer). The pack never decides who may be emailed.
The draft and sidecar never state that the email was sent, scheduled or that a list exists. Output is a draft for the existing approval path.
One next action, one link or one reply instruction. Multiple offers in one email are split into separate emails in the plan.
Offers, prices, dates and conditions appear only as in verifiedFacts.
Paragraphs of one to three sentences; the action visible without scrolling on a phone for short emails; respect the brief's limit.
rules.check: Paragraph lengths and word count recorded.

rules.instruction: Closing-soon and final-notice emails exist only when promotionWindow carries an approved end date; the deadline is stated exactly as approved. Scarcity claims need an approved quantity. Nothing is extended, reopened or 'brought back' by the copy.
rules.check: Every deadline or scarcity phrase matches the approved window.

rules.instruction: In any sequence, at least one email between asks delivers something useful on its own (a lesson, a resource from supportingAssets, an answer to a known objection) without a purchase ask beyond the standard footer.
rules.appliesWhen: Sequences of three or more emails.
rules.check: sequenceMap shows at least one value email between two ask emails.

rules.instruction: A postscript, if used, restates the single action or adds one true, useful detail; it never introduces a second offer, a new claim or urgency.
rules.check: PS content maps to the same action or an already-supported fact.

rules.instruction: Personalisation uses only placeholders the runtime supplies; the draft never invents a reader's name, company or history.

Return the exact campaign schema: emails with dayOffset, purpose, three distinct honest subjects, preview, plain-text body and the supplied single CTA. Match requested email count. Use no personalisation placeholders unless explicitly supplied. Draft dates are relative proposals, never scheduled sends.
rules.check: Count, allowed links, exact CTA, subject variety and day ordering validate.

qualityChecks.criterion: Every subject option is fulfilled by the body; no deceptive patterns.
No relationship or send-state claim beyond runtime data.
One action; terms match verified facts.

outputContract.customerFacing: Owner-reviewed campaign authoring and export only. No sending, recipient selection, scheduling or consent inference.
outputContract.internalSidecar: Sequence purpose and position, subject rationale, permission context used, omitted claims and findings.

examples.fictionalBrand: Fictional home-maintenance business (illustrative name: Bramble Home Care; every fact below is invented for illustration)
examples.inputScenario: Brief: second email in a 'new plan member' sequence, purpose: explain what happens at the first seasonal visit. permissionContext: existing customer. verifiedFacts: the visit checks heating, gutters, seals; duration 'about two hours' approved.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Subjects describe the first visit from different angles. Body opens with why they are receiving it (they joined the plan), lists the three checks and the approved duration, and ends with one action: reply with preferred weekday. No send claim.
examples.forbiddenBehaviour: 'Re: your booking' as a subject, inventing a technician's name, or adding an upsell offer with a price not in verified facts.

examples.fictionalBrand: Fictional B2B scheduling business (illustrative name: Slotwise; every fact below is invented for illustration)
examples.inputScenario: Brief: first email after trial sign-up, purpose: get the reader to connect their calendar. permissionContext: consented trial user. linkablePages includes the setup guide.
examples.expectedBehaviour: Subjects describe the setup step honestly. Body: why now (trial started), the one thing to do, what it enables (mechanism), one link to the setup guide.
examples.forbiddenBehaviour: Claiming 'most teams finish setup in 4 minutes' without a fact, or stating the email has been scheduled.
